tools_helpful.evidence: session-log: each UWP-only call carried a `// TODO[migrate-NNN]: see PATTERNS.md#getforcurrentview` marker (Scenario2_Disable.xaml.cs lines 27/34, Scenario3_AppCapture.xaml.cs line 33), which the agent used as its worklist.
CS1061 and WMC0909/WMC1111 from `dotnet build` (session-log ~2243-2247) precisely told the agent which API guesses were invalid, driving the fixes.

tool_limitations.limitation: `ApplicationView.GetForCurrentView().IsScreenCaptureEnabled` matched the generic `GetForCurrentView()` / `ApplicationView` patterns and was routed to PATTERNS.md#getforcurrentview, whose table only offers `AppWindow.GetFromWindowId(...)` — no coverage for the screen-capture-protection capability.
tool_limitations.suggested_tweak: Add a dedicated `IsScreenCaptureEnabled` adaptable pattern routed to a `screen-capture` anchor.

failed_apis.why_tried: Agent followed the windowing/GetForCurrentView guidance that maps ApplicationView → AppWindow and assumed the capture flag lived on AppWindow.
failed_apis.root_cause: WinUI 3 `AppWindow` has no `IsScreenCaptureEnabled` member; the UWP per-view capture flag has no AppWindow analog.
failed_apis.fix: Win32 P/Invoke `SetWindowDisplayAffinity(hwnd, WDA_EXCLUDEFROMCAPTURE)` on nav-in and `WDA_NONE` on nav-out, HWND from `WindowNative.GetWindowHandle(App.MainWindow!)`.

doc_errors.correct: Window-management members map to AppWindow, but `IsScreenCaptureEnabled` (content protection) does not — it needs Win32 `SetWindowDisplayAffinity`.

special_apis.special_handling: `AppCapture.GetForCurrentView()` may be unavailable at runtime; wrap in try/catch with a fallback status message. The static `AppCapture.SetAllowedAsync(bool)` still works for the toggle.

errors_encountered.fix: Switched the template to classic `{Binding Title}` (runtime binding, no x:DataType required).
